pizza-with-extra-meat-and-extra-vegetabl.title: Pizza with extra meat and extra vegetables, thin crust

content.title: About
content.content: A thin, crispy pizza topped with tomato sauce, a generous portion of extra meat (ham, sausage, chicken) and a variety of vegetables (bell pepper, onion, mushrooms, olives). Perfect for those who love hearty and flavorful dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The thin crust is made from high‑quality wheat flour and is allowed to rest for at least 24 hours for optimal flavor.
Extra meat is usually layered to keep it juicy throughout baking.
Vegetables are finely sliced to distribute evenly across the pizza surface.
Traditionally the pizza is baked at 250 °C for 8–10 minutes.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The thin crust and meat deliver quick energy, useful before active activities.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The abundance of meat and cheese makes the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑watching individuals.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salt in the sauce and processed meats can be high; people with hypertension should opt for a lower‑salt version.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The pizza may contain dairy, gluten, and meat ingredients that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into individual slices. Optionally garnish with fresh basil or arugula after baking for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crisp crust.

content.title: About
content.content: Quinoa is the seed of the plant Chenopodium quinoa, native to the Andes of South America. The seeds have a light nutty flavor, a soft texture when cooked, and are often used as a grain substitute.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quinoa was a staple food of the Incas and was called the "mother of all grains".
Quinoa is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.
It provides a complete protein, containing all nine essential amino acids.
There are several color varieties: white, red, and black quinoa.
Quinoa grows well at high altitudes and requires relatively little water.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Quinoa contains about 14 % protein and is considered a complete plant protein.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Quinoa provides magnesium, iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for bones and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Quinoa is rich in quercetin and kaempferol, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Quinoa raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Saponin content
items.content: Saponins can cause mild stomach irritation; thorough rinsing before cooking is recommended.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to quinoa.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking reduces its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook quinoa in a 1:2 ratio of quinoa to water for 15‑20 minutes until tender. It can be added to salads, soups, side dishes, used in vegetarian patties, or served as a breakfast base with fruit and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry quinoa in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth.

yogurt-greek-low-fat-milk-flavors-other-.title: Greek Yogurt, Low Fat Milk, Non‑Fruit Flavors

content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt made from low‑fat milk is a thick, creamy dairy product created by straining regular yogurt. Unlike fruit‑flavored versions, this product uses flavorings such as vanilla, honey, caramel, or spice blends, giving it a neutral and versatile taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt contains two to three times more protein than regular yogurt.
Straining removes most of the whey, concentrating nutrients.
Low‑fat milk retains most of the calcium while reducing fat content.
Non‑fruit flavors often rely on natural extracts and a touch of honey for sweetness.
Greek yogurt is frequently used as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise in recipes.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: One cup (200 ml) provides about 20 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Using low‑fat milk makes the product virtually fat‑free, suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium is essential for bone and teeth health; 200 ml supplies roughly 15 % of the daily value.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Live cultures such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium promote gut health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Greek yogurt raises blood sugar slowly, making it a good choice for diabetics.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy should avoid the product.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Some flavorings may contain artificial sweeteners; check the label if you avoid them.

items.title: Potential sodium content
items.content: Certain flavored versions can include salt; choose a low‑sodium option if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Non‑fruit Greek yogurt works well as a breakfast with nuts and honey, in smoothies, as a dip or sauce, and as a sour‑cream substitute in baking and savory dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 2‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.
